PART-H DECISIONS AND REASONS 21.
The claim, reply, documents and the evidence led on record by both the parties has been considered.

The issues to be decided in the present case are (1) Whether the workman himself had stopped to report for duty due to his disability he received in road accident and was not in a position to work and requested the management for his pension from ESI department which was being paid to him?

OPM (2) Whether the services of the Chanderpal Vs. M/s Capital Bus Service Pvt. Ltd.

22. Decision regarding issue No.1:
The onus to prove issue no. 1 was upon the management.

The management had claimed in its written statement that the workman had met with a road accident and he had received a huge amount of compensation under MV Act for the disability sustained by him on account of the road accident from the concerned insurance company.

Due to the said disability, the workman was not in a position to work with the management, so, he himself stopped reporting for duty and requested the management for his pension from ESI Department, which is being paid to him.
However, in the evidence affidavit filed on behalf of the management, the management has chose to stay silent on this aspect, entirely.
It has not mentioned anything about the workman availing retirement benefits from ESIC Department on account of his disability.

Rather, in the evidence affidavit of the management, the management has stated that after leaving the employment of the management, the workman is gainfully employed and earning handsomely.
23.
Thus, the management has not brought any cogent or positive evidence to prove the aforesaid issue and has failed to discharge the onus of proof placed upon it in this regard.

Therefore, by failing to bring on record any evidence, the management has failed to prove the said issue and has also remained silent on the said aspect completely in the evidence affidavit filed on behalf of management vide Ex.MW1/A, issue Chanderpal Vs. M/s Capital Bus Service Pvt. Ltd. no. 1 is decided in favour of the workman and against the management.

sentences.text: Issue No. 2 - Whether the services of the workman have been terminated illegally and/or unjustifiably by the management?
OPW Decision regarding issue No.2:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of D.K.Yadav Vs. J.M.A.Industries Ltd. (1993 SCC (L&S) 723) has also held as under:
The order of termination of the service of an employee/workman visits with civil consequences of jeopardising not only his/her livelihood but also career and livelihood of dependents.

Therefore, before taking any action putting an end to the tenure of an employee/workman, fair play requires that a reasonable opportunity to put forth his case is given and domestic enquiry conducted complying with the principles of natural justice.
25. The onus to prove the disability of the workman to continue working with the management was upon the management.
The management has taken the stand that they never terminated the services of the workman, but it is the workman himself who has abandoned his employment on account of his disability.
As already decided above, the management has failed to prove that the workman was unfit for service and had stopped reporting for duty on account of his disability.

The contention of the AR of the workman is that the service of the workman has been terminated illegally by the management, without issuing any notice or memo to the workman or holding an enquiry against the workman.
26. In his cross-examination, the claimant deposed that he was Chanderpal Vs. M/s Capital Bus Service Pvt. Ltd. employed as a checker with the management since 01.01.2004.

27. The witness for the management, in his cross-examination, admitted that the workman had joined the management on 01.01.2004 as a checker and that it was the management who used to maintain the attendance register as well as the payment register.
The management used to mark attendance of the workman on the attendance register.
The name of the workman was still on record of the management.
He stated that he could produce the attendance record of the workman but the management never produced the attendance records of the workman before the court.

Thus,
admittedly it was the management who had the physical custody of the said attendance registers and could maintain them as they liked.
It was up to them to mark the presence/ absence of the workman as per their whims and fancies and the management never produced the said attendance records of the workman.
28. The witness for the management had also stated that the management had sent call letters to the workman to join duty but failed to produce any such call letter on record.

Though the workman in his statement of claim has alleged no domestic inquiry was conducted against him by the management and his job was terminated illegally without issuing any notice to him, the management has chosen to remain silent on this aspect, simply stating that it had never terminated the services of the workman.

MW-1, though in his cross-examination has admitted Chanderpal Vs.
M/s Capital Bus Service Pvt. Ltd. that no domestic enquiry was conducted by the management against the workman.

29. When the workman failed to join back the service and report for duty on account of his disability, as is contended by the management, and this scenario continued, it could not have been possible for the management to believe that the workman would join back.
However, the management has claimed that it had not terminated services of the workman.
Management did not prove on record any of the call back notices which it claims were sent to the workman for not reporting to duty.

Till the date of his termination, the management had never issued any notice or initiated any domestic inquiry against the workman for such prolonged absence (on account of his disability), which would ordinarily have been construed as a misconduct on part of the workman.

30. Hence, the version of the management that it was the workman who had remained absent for so long and had refused to join work, cannot be believed, in absence of any such notice or domestic inquiry against the workman, more so when the management has not been able to produce any letter issued to the workman to join back on work, especially considering that they Chanderpal Vs.
M/s Capital Bus Service Pvt. Ltd. were having the custody and were maintaining the attendance registers the entire time and the workman was never required to mark his absence/ presence in the said register by himself.

sentences.text:
This conduct of the management shows that even though no termination letter was ever issued to the workman, effectively, the services of the workman were terminated by the management and that too illegally and unjustifiably, without issuing any notice to the workman or conducting any inquiry against him with regard to the alleged misconduct on part of the workman of his continued absenteeism.
31.

As far as the contention that neither any notice was issued by the management nor any internal inquiry was conducted against the workman by the management for the alleged misconduct, this Court is of the opinion that such inquiry is only required when the management intends to inflict some punishment upon the workman.

Well, this punishment was inflicted upon the workman as he has effectively and constructively been terminated from the services of the management, w.e.f.
December, 2019.
The management should have held an enquiry in such a case, which they have failed to do.
Accordingly, issue no. 2 is decided against the management and in favour of the workman.

It is held that the management had illegally and/or unjustifiably terminated the services of the workman without issuing any notice or holding any domestic inquiry against the workman for the alleged misconduct of continued absenteeism on part of the workman.

sentences.text: As far as relief part is concerned, the workman has made a prayer in statement of claim that an award may be passed in his favour and against the management holding his termination from work as illegal and directing the management to reinstate him in service with continuity of service and with full back wages and all consequential benefits along with costs.
However, the workman has already admitted in his cross-examination that even on date, he is being provided the pension benefits by ESIC Department and his monthly pension is about Rs. 6,200/-.
Therefore, the workman, in this case cannot claim reinstatement or relief of back wages as a matter of right.

34. On this point, this court finds support from the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation, Jaipur v Phool Chand (D) Through Lrs.1, in which it was held that "In our considered opinion, the Courts below completely failed to see that the back wages could not be awarded by the Court as of right to the workman consequent upon setting aside of his dismissal/termination order.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, a workman has no right to claim back wages from his employer as of right only because the Court has set aside his dismissal order in his favour and directed his reinstatement in service."
1 Civil Appeal No.1756 of 2010 (date of decision 20.09.2018) Chanderpal Vs.
M/s Capital Bus Service Pvt. Ltd.

It further held that It is necessary for the workman in such cases to plead and prove with the aid of evidence that after his dismissal from the service, he was not gainfully employed anywhere and had no earning to maintain himself or/and his family.
The employer is also entitled to prove it otherwise against the employee, namely, that the employee was gainfully employed during the relevant period and hence not entitled to claim any back wages.
Initial burden is, however, on the employee."

It further held that "In some cases, the Court may decline to award the back wages in its entirety whereas in some cases, it may award partial depending upon the facts of each case by exercising its judicial discretion in the light of the facts and evidence.

The questions, how the back wages is required to be decided, what are the factors to be taken into consideration awarding back wages, on whom the initial burden lies etc. were elaborately discussed in several cases by this Court wherein the law on these questions has been settled.
Indeed, it is no longer res integra.

36. The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case titled as Indian Hydraulic Industries Pvt. Ltd v. Krishan Devi and Bhagwati Devi & Ors.2 has held that "even if the termination of a person is held illegal,
Labour Court is not supposed to direct reinstatement along with full back wages and the relief can be moulded according to the facts and circumstances of each case.

entities.text: Indian Hydraulic Industries Pvt. Ltd v. Krishan Devi and Bhagwati Devi & Ors.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court has to adopt a pragmatic approach and take into account the allegations made by the work-women, the nature of contribution by the work-women to the industry, the time gap and averments made about the unemployment and proof of unemployment as the relevant factors to be considered in such cases.

The Labor Court can allow compensation to the workman instead of reinstatement and back wages."
37.

In K.V Anil Mithra and Anr. v. The contention of the AR of the workman is that the service of the workman has been terminated illegally by the management, without issuing any notice or memo to the workman or holding an enquiry against the workman.
It was up to them to mark the presence/ absence of the workman as per their whims and fancies and the management never produced the said attendance records of the workman.
Though the workman in his statement of claim has alleged no domestic inquiry was conducted against him by the management and his job was terminated illegally without issuing any notice to him, the management has chosen to remain silent on this aspect, simply stating that it had never terminated the services of the workman.
However, the management has claimed that it had not terminated services of the workman.
Management did not prove on record any of the call back notices which it claims were sent to the workman for not reporting to duty.
Till the date of his termination, the management had never issued any notice or initiated any domestic inquiry against the workman for such prolonged absence (on account of his disability), which would ordinarily have been construed as a misconduct on part of the workman.
30. Hence, the version of the management that it was the workman who had remained absent for so long and had refused to join work, cannot be believed, in absence of any such notice or domestic inquiry against the workman, more so when the management has not been able to produce any letter issued to the workman to join back on work, especially considering that they Chanderpal Vs.
M/s Capital Bus Service Pvt. Ltd. were having the custody and were maintaining the attendance registers the entire time and the workman was never required to mark his absence/ presence in the said register by himself.
This conduct of the management shows that even though no termination letter was ever issued to the workman, effectively, the services of the workman were terminated by the management and that too illegally and unjustifiably, without issuing any notice to the workman or conducting any inquiry against him with regard to the alleged misconduct on part of the workman of his continued absenteeism.
